## Overview

Hybrid bounds combine multiple methods to achieve tighter confidence bands:

- **Simes method**: Tighter in the upper tail
- **Dempster method**: Tighter in the lower tail
- **DKW method**: Tighter in the middle

```{r load}
library(dkw)
```

## Comparing DKW and Hybrid Bands

```{r compare-bands}
set.seed(123)

# Generate uniform sample
n <- 200
x <- sort(runif(n))
Fhat <- ecdf(x)(x)

# Compute both band types
dkw <- dkw_band(Fhat, alpha = 0.05, n = n)
hybrid <- hybrid_band(Fhat, alpha = 0.05, m = n)
```

## Visualization

```{r plot-comparison}
plot(x, Fhat, type = "s", lwd = 2,
     ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "x", ylab = "F(x)",
     main = "DKW vs Hybrid Confidence Bands")

# DKW bands (gray dashed)
lines(x, dkw$lower, col = "gray50", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
lines(x, dkw$upper, col = "gray50", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

# Hybrid bands (red solid)
lines(x, hybrid$lower, col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(x, hybrid$upper, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# True CDF
abline(0, 1, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

legend("bottomright",
       c("ECDF", "DKW Bands", "Hybrid Bands", "True CDF"),
       col = c("black", "gray50", "red", "blue"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 1, 1), lwd = 2)
```

## Where Hybrid Bands Are Tighter

```{r improvement}
# Compute improvement
improvement_lower <- hybrid$lower - dkw$lower
improvement_upper <- dkw$upper - hybrid$upper

# Plot improvement
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(x, improvement_lower, type = "l",
     main = "Lower Bound Improvement",
     xlab = "x", ylab = "Hybrid - DKW",
     col = "blue", lwd = 2)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

plot(x, improvement_upper, type = "l",
     main = "Upper Bound Improvement",
     xlab = "x", ylab = "DKW - Hybrid",
     col = "red", lwd = 2)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```
